text:
alisa: Heads up — ran into a routing edge with the new region-pref policy. Local affinity works but when local is full it falls back to east instead of nearest healthy zone.

dmitri: hmm, is the fallback order using region distance or zone weight? should be latency-first then capacity.

alisa: according to the live policy config it reads: fallback: [region_preference, capacity_weight]. but the console UI says 'latency-based' when enabled. mismatch. :grimacing:

jen: could be a serialization bug on rollout. Did the canary CV write the same policy as console preview?

sam: @jen I saw the preview show "nearest_if_latency_under: 120ms" but runtime used a hard region list. I can reproduce locally with curl + X-Geo-Hint header.

luca: paste the headers you used? we added header pass-through and override precedence last week. might be related.

sam: sure — request: 

```
GET /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
X-Client-Region: eu-west-1
X-Fallback-Policy: prefer-latency
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
```

response routing header: `X-Served-Region: us-east-1` — wrong; eu-central was closer and had capacity.

dmitri: can you dump the evaluated policy from the gateway for that request? the runtime logs an "eval_plan" when DEBUG is on.

sam: turned on DEBUG for 30s, grabbed a trace:

```
route_match: /v1/* -> backend: inference-v2
policy: region_preference: local, fallback_order: [region_list]
evaluator: header_override_detected -> use_header: true
resolved_candidates: [eu-central, eu-west-1, us-east-1]
selected: us-east-1 (reason: header_override_priority=high)
```

jen: ah — header_override_priority=high. That sounds like the console flag that treats X-Client-Region as authoritative for tenancy. Should default to hint only, not override.

alisa: this is the UX/console thing: when "allow header override" is toggled in the UI we show 'Accepts client region hints' but that ambiguous wording lets teams think it's a soft hint. We need to change labels and the rollout semantics.

luca: agreed. Proposed fix: two modes — `hint` and `strict`. `hint` adds candidate boost; `strict` rewrites routing precedence and short-circuits fallback. Default to `hint`.

dmitri: code-level: in route evaluator, header_override_priority currently maps to enum {low, normal, high}. We should replace with mode enum and make the default 'hint'. Also add telemetry flag `header_mode` to per-request traces.

sam: I'll open a tiny PR to change the enum and add telemetry fields. Do we also want a console patch to rename the toggle and add a confirmation?

jen: yes — UX: show a tooltip: "Hint: clients can suggest a region; Strict: clients can force selection and bypass fallback policies." And add a warning when enabling strict for public APIs.

alisa: add a quota note too — strict route could be used to concentrate traffic on a zone and blow past reserved capacity. We should surface quota warnings in console when enabling strict.

luca: good catch. telemetry items: add event `route.header_mode.set` and metric `header_mode.strict_requests` + sample of selected_region vs nearest_region to detect suspicious concentration.

dmitri: work items:
- sam: PR to runtime enum + telemetry (small) — owner: sam — due: 2d
- jen: console copy + warning + confirm modal — owner: jen — due: 3d
- luca: create alert/metric in observability for concentration — owner: luca — due: 4d
- alisa: update docs and runbook to explain hint vs strict — owner: alisa — due: 5d

sam: opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1728 — includes tests and a tiny config migration shim. :tada:

infra-bot: deploy triggered for branch sam/header-mode -> staging at rev: 7a3d2f3 (ETA ~8m)

dmitri: once staging passes, let's canary to eu-west with 10% and monitor header_mode.strict_requests.

jen: UX question — should the console default to `hint` on existing tenants or only for new? migrating existing tenants might change behavior.

alisa: do NOT change existing tenants silently. migration path must be opt-in and surfaced in the rollout tab with a diff preview of evaluated policy.

sam: noted. PR updated to include a migration flag and a log line when tenant config lacks header_mode (treat as legacy -> preserve current behavior).

luca: OK - I'll add a telemetry dashboard tile that shows legacy vs explicit header_mode usage per-tenant.

jen: thanks all. I'll draft the console copy and add the confirm modal mockups to the PR.

alisa: thanks — great catch. we'll post a short note in #eng-updates when canary goes live. :thumbsup:
